The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test case attempts to validate the behavior of the method `ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)` when merging arrays of different but related generic types (e.g., Integer[] and Long[], both subclasses of Number[]). The test succeeds when merging `Number[]` arrays, but when merging an `Integer[]` with a `Long[]` array, it expects an `IllegalArgumentException`.

Inspecting the implementation of `addAll(T[] array1, T... array2)` reveals the following process:
- If either array is null, it returns a clone of the other.
- It retrieves the component type of the first array (`type1`).
- It creates a new array of type `type1` with length equal to the sum of the input array lengths.
- It copies the contents of `array1` and `array2` into the new array using `System.arraycopy`.

The issue is that the method only considers the component type of the first array when creating the new array. If the second array has elements incompatible with this type, the `System.arraycopy` triggers `ArrayStoreException` at runtime (e.g., storing Long in Integer[]). This exception is not very descriptive compared to the intended `IllegalArgumentException` to signal incompatible array types.

The current behavior does not perform any explicit checks for type compatibility before array copying. This leads to runtime exceptions that are not intuitive for the user.

The bug report points out this exact problem and suggests that a more user-friendly exception would be helpful, such as throwing an `IllegalArgumentException` when the types are incompatible, rather than letting the system throw a generic `ArrayStoreException`.

Recent bug reports do not touch on similar issues and hence do not provide additional relevant context.

Summary: The bug arises because `addAll` only checks the component type of the first array and does not validate that the second array elements are compatible before performing `System.arraycopy`, resulting in confusing `ArrayStoreException`. The code should verify type compatibility between arrays and throw a clearer exception if incompatible before copying.

This explains the failure of the test, which expects an `IllegalArgumentException` but instead gets an `ArrayStoreException` from the system copy operation.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
